metadata.title: HPC Federated Access Trust

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for governing federated and external identity access to high-performance computing platforms while preserving attribution, accountability, and trust boundaries.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Federated identity systems, external job submission interfaces, cross-institution HPC collaboration frameworks, and shared scheduling environments.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern for defining trust boundaries and governance expectations when external or federated identities access HPC platforms.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Federated access relies on HPC-specific job attribution, scheduler-mediated authorization, and role separation.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Federated access requires a trusted enterprise identity foundation for external identity verification, federation, and lifecycle governance.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Federated collaboration, external identity attribution, and access boundary considerations as defined in NIST SP 800-234.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Federated users and external collaborators are valid accounts whose misuse represents a primary HPC threat model.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Persistence or privilege manipulation risks arising from federated account misconfiguration.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit enforcement of trust boundaries between internal and federated identities.

metadata.remarks: HPC Federated Access Trust formalizes the trust assumptions and governance boundaries required when external or cross-institution identities access HPC resources. This pattern does not implement enforcement mechanisms itself; instead, it constrains how identity, job lifecycle, and monitoring patterns must be composed to preserve attribution, accountability, and risk awareness in federated HPC environments.

components.title: Federated Identity Attribution
components.description: Ensures externally authenticated identities are mapped to durable, attributable HPC principals for job execution and accountability.

components.title: Federated Trust Boundary Definition
components.description: Defines explicit boundaries between internal and federated identities, including scoped privileges, constrained access, and differentiated trust assumptions.

components.title: Federated Access Accountability
components.description: Ensures federated users and jobs are subject to attribution, monitoring, and revocation equivalent to internal users.
